summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-R5 admits no external crate. academic-repository-competency links academic-domain, academic-policy, academic-repository-analysis, academic-repository-classification, academic-repository-correlation and thiserror as product edges, and academic-model-run, academic-repository, academic-untrusted-content and trybuild as dev edges, all covered by earlier reviewed receipts, and adds one workspace path package. Nothing links into a product binary that was not already there: the five workspace product edges are path packages this repository already builds, and thiserror was admitted by the phase 1 receipt. Build-time-only additions are zero -- there is no build script, no proc macro beyond thiserror's, and no code generator.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-repository-competency is the P2-R5 boundary: section 17.6's separation of ProjectSnapshot OBSERVES Concept from User APPLIED Concept. It owns the authorship identity mapping, the scaffold-versus-meaningful-change rubric as versioned configuration, the three-step warrant generated code needs before it may found a personal claim, the read-versus-authored boundary held as two disjoint vocabularies, and the two claims' independent identities and provenance. It is a separate package from academic-repository-classification because that crate owns what the snapshot contains and this one owns what the user did, and the direction of the edge is what keeps a classification constructible without a promotion and a promotion impossible without a classification.

no_second_ladder_note: Section 17.3's evidence ladder was implemented by P2-R2, section 17.5's seven relations by P2-R3 and section 18's three classifications by P2-R4, and this task adds none of them again. A ProjectObservationClaim is read out of a P2-R4 ConceptStance's observed half and from nothing else, so there is no route from repository bytes to a personal claim that skips any of the four crates below. What this task adds is not a fourth ladder but a second claim: a PersonalApplicationClaim needs, beside that observation, a sealed AuthoredWork whose own changed sites meet the observation's locators, and AuthoredWork has one producer, ContributionDraft::seal, which applies section 17.6's five checks.

direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: MasteryLevel. A personal claim is offered at section 13.1's APPLIED and never above it, because that section's FLUENT row is `AI 단독 판정 금지` and its APPLIED row's ceiling note is `dependency 설치만으로 금지`. The level is read from the shared vocabulary rather than restated here.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-policy: ContentDigest, for the two claim identities. Each is a domain-separated digest over the facts it binds, in two different domains, rather than those facts joined: ClaimId admits 64 bytes, a snapshot identifier is most of that, and a joined identity truncated to fit would drop the last fact and make two claims differing only there one identity. That is the defect P2-R4 shipped and measured in its own requirement identity, and it is this Run's P2-A1 P1 shape -- content standing in for identity, with the collision silent.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-analysis: P2-R2's Locator and PathClass. A ChangedSite is built over a P2-R2 locator, whose constructor is crate-private to that crate, so a contribution cannot name a place the analyzer never saw; the work-to-observation join compares P2-R2's own span-independent SymbolFingerprint; and the scaffold rubric's path half reuses PathClass rather than introducing a second vocabulary for source this repository did not write.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-classification: P2-R4's ClassificationSet, ConceptStance, ClassificationKey and ObservedProof. The project claim is the observed half of a stance and the personal claim is bound to the same key, so the two claims are about one subject and are two values.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-correlation: P2-R3's EvidenceRelation, which a project claim's provenance carries so a reader can see which of section 17.5's relations observed the use. It arrives through P2-R4's ObservedProof and is not re-derived.

dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-model-run: CalibrationRegistry and its dataset types, to build the fresh calibration P2-R2's OBSERVED rungs require before a finding exists to classify and promote from.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository: P2-R1's capture_local, SnapshotRequest and the identity types a request carries, so every corpus in the acceptance suite is a frozen snapshot that passed the permission and secret gate rather than a fabricated one.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-untrusted-content: SourceIndex, which P2-R1's capture_local returns and P2-R2's AnalysisInput::of checks every unit against.
dev_workspace_dependencies.trybuild: The compile-fail suite. Section 17.6's separations are types, and the seven cases under crates/repository-competency/tests/compile_fail assert that each refusal is a program that does not compile with a committed diagnostic -- a review that has no authorship spelling, a warrant with a step skipped, a generated origin with the warrant left out, and an eligible contribution or a personal claim written past the checks that would have produced it. The cases live in this package rather than in academic-scenario's suite, where P2-R2's went, for P2-R4's reason: this crate reaches academic-ledger through P2-R3 and scenario_crate_has_no_writer_dependency refuses academic-scenario that crate through a dev edge as much as a product one.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-repository-competency is a workspace path crate, not an external dependency. It owns section 17.6, whose whole content is that using a repository is not a personal claim: AuthorshipMap::resolve is whole-pair set membership over the identities the user recorded, so an author string that is nearly the user's -- the same address in another namespace, the same address in another case, a display name that reads like them -- resolves to nobody; ScaffoldRubric is a caller-supplied versioned value with no Default and no numeric literal in its judgement, so the scaffold-versus-meaningful line is configuration a reader can see rather than a threshold compiled in; ContributionKind::authorship_mode is the one door from what a connector reports to what a claim serializes and answers None for REVIEWED and READ, and AuthorshipMode has no variant for either, so a review has no spelling in the authorship field at all; CodeOrigin::Generated holds a GeneratedCodeWarrant whose three steps each take the previous by value, so generated code the user never modified is a program that does not compile rather than a value that validates badly; and the two claims carry independent domain-separated digest identities and independent provenance, so rejecting the personal one leaves the project one untouched. Its dependency set is minimal and the edges it does not have are the point: no academic-store, so a promotion cannot reach the canonical writer and adds no migration; no academic-worker and no academic-egress-boundary, so nothing in its closure can launch a process or stage a payload.
network_posture: The crate opens no socket, opens no file, declares no foreign function, reads no environment variable, spawns no process, and runs no build script. It spells no std::fs name at all: every artifact arrives as an argument, the way P2-R3's documents and P2-R4's chains do. the_competency_crate_touches_no_file_and_no_socket in crates/repository-competency/tests/competency_scans.rs compares the whole set of its use items, the whole set of the two-segment paths it reaches through a crate root -- one, thiserror::Error -- and the whole set of the macros it invokes -- one, matches! -- against pinned inventories in both directions, and runs a whole-identifier pass for filesystem and transport constructs over every file of the package, tests included. every_field_of_this_crate_is_in_the_inventory compares all 100 declared fields against a pinned inventory in both directions and requires each to say which of eight things it holds, so a field carrying analyzed bytes under a name no alternation lists appears as an extra key. Its link closure holds nothing that can open a socket beyond libc, which reaches it through academic-policy's bundled SQLite by way of academic-repository. Every snapshot, corpus, contribution, mapping, rubric, warrant and outcome in its test tree is synthetic and built in process; no real repository is read, no version-control command is run, and no network call is made.
advisory_path: Unchanged. Every external crate academic-repository-competency links was admitted by an earlier receipt and is triaged through that receipt's advisory path. trybuild is a dev dependency already admitted for academic-scenario, academic-desktop, academic-proposal and academic-repository-classification. .github/dependabot.yml opens no version-update pull request.
